  home? `.git` file -> yes (pointer to a repository elsewhere); `.git` directory -> yes only with
  `HEAD`; nothing there -> no; dangling symlink -> yes (fail closed); unreadable -> yes (fail closed).
  That last pair is what keeps #6673's guarantee: the only shapes that stop refusing are ones git
  itself walks past because they are not repositories.
- The refusal set is provably a strict subset of the old one: everything that used to refuse still
  does except a directory named `.git` with no `HEAD`, which cannot hold a `meta.json` git could
  restore.

  no error-code change, no second copy of the rule (C-001, C-002).
